The only public pick record is WagerTalk's own Last 20 list, and a forum member's tally of this season's newsletter Key Releases is under 50%.

short_answer: The Gold Sheet is a real and very old product. A 2019 press release and WagerTalk's own pages say it was founded in 1957, and a Chicago Sun-Times story names Mort Olshan as its founder. Since the 2026 season it has been sold only at WagerTalk, which bought it after announcing the deal in May 2019. You get what is advertised: a weekly football paper with write ups, power ratings and logs for every NFL and FBS game, and a daily basketball paper.

Whether its picks make money is another question. WagerTalk sells separate LTS picks and advertises hot runs such as 52-25 (+80.63) in the last 77 football plays. The only record we could open is the Last 20 list on the same page: 12 wins and 8 losses from 11 to 16 Nov 2026. At one unit a play, by our count, that is about +1.9 units. The page says +12.23 units and does not show play sizes, so we could not reproduce that figure. A TheRX member who tracks newsletter picks at the printed lines had this season's Key Releases at 17-27 in college and 21-20-1 in the NFL through 9 Nov 2026.
Treat the newsletter as research you pay for, not as a record you can bank on. The pick guarantee returns WagerTalk credit, not money, and the refund policy says all sales are final.

guarantee: Only single picks bought with the guaranteed option carry a promise, and it is a credit. WagerTalk's wording: "If your daily pick(s) package does not result in an overall profit across all included plays, the paid cash value of a guaranteed pick will be credited back to your account to be used on a future purchase." The guaranteed version costs more ($8 instead of $5 on the sale prices we saw, $38 instead of $25 at list).

Everything else is final. WagerTalk's refund policy says "All Sales are Final and products are sold "as is"." Its terms add that the company's entire liability and the buyer's "exclusive remedy" is "a refund of the price paid or replacement of our products, at our option." We saw no refund terms for the newsletters or the passes.
No option covers what you lose on the bets themselves.

claims_note: The newsletter and the paid picks are two different products. The newsletter carries Key Releases, Tech Plays and other rated plays printed on Tuesday. The LTS picks are released later, after line moves and injury news, and the hot streak numbers in the ads refer to those LTS picks. A good LTS run does not tell you how the newsletter plays did, and the other way round.

The ads quote records over windows that change from ad to ad (last 13, last 77, last 145, last 185, since October, since last September). Picking the window after the fact is a common way to make a record look better. Ask for the full log instead.
record: Watchdog graded sample, new 22 Nov 2026. The Gold Sheet does not publish a complete, time stamped log we can audit, so we built a sample from public posts that carry their plays. Watchdog captures X accounts and forum threads that post or repost picks; the ones naming The Gold Sheet most often were BuzzKill (TheRX newsletters thread), jillmark, WagerTalkPicks, 1218Sports. From 19 Sep 2026 to 21 Nov 2026 we took every play our parser could read inside a The Gold Sheet block, kept only those posted before the game started, removed repeats, and graded each one against the final score at one unit risked, at the odds shown or -110 when none were shown.

Result: 25 plays, 16 won, 9 lost, +5.19 units, a return of +20.7% per unit risked. By sport: NCAAF 12 won, 8 lost, +2.87 units; NBA 2 won, 1 lost, +0.50 units. By month: September 3 won, 0 lost, +2.73 units; October 8 won, 5 lost, +2.23 units; November 5 won, 4 lost, +0.22 units.

What it means: a 64% win rate on 25 decided plays has a 95% range of about 45% to 80%, and at the prices in this sample a bettor needed about 53% to break even. That range includes break even, so this sample cannot show whether they win or lose over time. The sample covers only the plays that others chose to post, which is not the full card a subscriber receives, and stakes are counted flat even where the seller rates plays differently.

What is independently verifiable: nothing complete. We found no third party log of every LTS pick, no contest standings and no regulator or court record in our searches. The closest thing is a member of TheRX forum who grades many newsletters each week at the line printed in the paper, not the closing line. On 9 Nov 2026 that tally had The Gold Sheet's Key Releases at 17-27 in college football and 21-20-1 in the NFL, a combined 38-47-1 (44.7%). It had college Tech Plays at 5-6-1, NFL Tech Plays at 7-2, and Priority Picks at 2-4 (college) and 3-1 (NFL). The same tally listed last season's college Tech Plays at 14-3 among its best records. We did not check these numbers against the papers.

What the seller itself publishes: WagerTalk's Last 20 list for GoldSheet showed date, sport, pick, price and result for 20 plays from 11 to 16 Nov 2026. We counted 12 wins and 8 losses (60%): 8-3 in football (6-0 college, 2-3 NFL) and 4-5 in basketball. Risking one unit on every play at the listed prices, our count comes to about +1.94 units. The page says +12.23 units, so plays must be sized differently, but the list does not say how. The same list shows the losses, which is more than many sellers show.
WagerTalk is both the store and the scorekeeper for these picks, so every number above except the forum tally comes from the company that sells them.

customers_intro: Most of what we found is forum talk among long time newsletter readers on Sportsbook Review, Covers and TheRX, plus a forum member's weekly tally. We found no review site sample we could count, and our Reddit search was partial because the archive we use kept timing out.

customers.text: We found about a dozen relevant posts on Sportsbook Review, Covers and TheRX from 2020 to 2026. The pattern is consistent: bettors respect The Gold Sheet as a long running source of data and ideas, and doubt its picks. One reader of decades praised its writer, another said it gave them great ideas, and one recalled reading it on newsstands in the 1980s. On the other side, one member called it worthless and said you cannot win with it over time, and a TheRX member disliked the 2026 format. A forum member's tally of this season's newsletter Key Releases was below 50% in college and about even in the NFL through 9 Nov 2026, while the same tally rated last season's college Tech Plays among the best. Several posts show readers sharing copies of the paper for free on forums.

A Sportsbook Review member who said they had bet football for decades listed The Gold Sheet first among the newsletters they read and praised its writer by name. They added that they rarely play newsletter picks and reads them for information.
In the same thread another member called The Gold Sheet very bad, said it was not worth the paper it was printed on, and said there was no way to win with it on a regular basis.
A third member recalled going to newsstands in the 1980s with friends to read The Gold Sheet, and said the sellers wanted people to pay before reading it.
In a Covers thread about another newsletter, a member said they used to get The Gold Sheet and "loved it", saying it gave them great ideas.

A TheRX member who grades newsletter picks at the printed line posted The Gold Sheet's 2026 record through 9 Nov: Key Releases 17-27 in college and 21-20-1 in the NFL, Tech Plays 5-6-1 and 7-2, Priority Picks 2-4 and 3-1. The same post listed last season's college Tech Plays at 14-3 among the best records. We did not verify the tally.
The same weekly tally was reposted on Sportsbook Review, with the same Gold Sheet numbers.

On TheRX a member asked where the Tech Plays were in the new Gold Sheet and called the format awful. In the same exchange a long time poster noted that Gold Sheet plays and newsletters are not allowed in the forum's Service Plays section.

In the 2024 season the TheRX tally had The Gold Sheet's college Key Releases at 4-7 through 14 Oct, and the member who keeps it said the paper's picks used to all be labeled Key Releases before they split them into categories.
A TheRX member asked whether The Gold Sheet could still be had without going through WagerTalk. We saw no answer on that page.
On Sportsbook Review a member pointed another bettor to Gold Sheet samples and noted that all GoldSheet newsletter content was available at WagerTalk, describing it as strictly for handicapping.

We found no Better Business Bureau profile we could confirm, no app store listing and no customer testimonials on the GoldSheet pages we read. Our Reddit search was partial: the archive's full text search timed out, and our saved Reddit posts held no real discussion of The Gold Sheet.

conflicts: WagerTalk sells The Gold Sheet's picks, grades them and publishes the leaderboard the ads quote. The scorekeeper and the store are the same company.
The Gold Sheet is one of many handicappers sold at WagerTalk, whose parent WagerTalk Media also runs SportsMemo. The GoldSheet hub links to the full WagerTalk roster of other paid handicappers.
strengths: A long history with outside paper trail: a 2019 press release and a 2020 corporate announcement describe the purchase and ownership, and a Sun-Times story names its founder.
Cheap ways to sample: a free football issue (the 3 Nov 2026 edition was open), a $19 single football issue and a free basketball single issue on the day we checked.
A Last 20 list with the actual line, odds and result for each LTS pick, including the losses.
The newsletter covers every NFL and FBS game each week with power ratings, logs and stat comparisons, which forum readers value as research.
concerns: Hot streak claims over hand picked windows (last 13, last 77, last 185) with no full log to check them.
The +12.23 unit figure on the Last 20 could not be reproduced; at one unit a play we got about +1.9 units.
The guarantee returns credit, not cash, and only on the higher priced guaranteed picks. All other sales are final.
A forum member's tally of this season's printed Key Releases was 38-47-1 through 9 Nov 2026, well below the 52.4% needed to break even at -110.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is a real, long running newsletter, founded in 1957 according to WagerTalk and a 2019 press release, and now sold by WagerTalk Media. That makes it a legitimate business. Whether its picks win over time is not shown: the only record we could open is WagerTalk's own Last 20 list.
What does the Watchdog sample of The Gold Sheet show?

We graded 25 of their plays that were posted publicly before the game started, 19 Sep 2026 to 21 Nov 2026: 16 won, 9 lost, +5.19 units at one unit each. The 95% range of the win rate is about 45% to 80%, against about 53% needed to break even.
How much does The Gold Sheet cost?

On 17 Nov 2026 the football newsletter was $79 for the season or $19 an issue, the basketball newsletter $179 a season, $39 for 30 days or $19 for 7 days, and the combo $229. LTS picks were $5 each on sale ($25 list), or $8 guaranteed, and passes ran from $39 a day to $1,999 a year.
Does The Gold Sheet have a verified record?

No. WagerTalk shows a Last 20 list (12-8 from 11 to 16 Nov 2026) and season claims, all graded by the company that sells the picks. A TheRX member's tally of this season's newsletter Key Releases was 17-27 in college and 21-20-1 in the NFL through 9 Nov 2026.
What is the difference between the newsletter and the LTS picks?

The newsletter is published Tuesday nights in football season (daily for basketball) with analysis and rated plays for every game. The LTS picks are a separate paid product released later in the week, after line moves and injury news. The hot streak numbers in WagerTalk's ads are about the LTS picks.
Does The Gold Sheet offer refunds?
No cash refunds. WagerTalk's refund policy says all sales are final. Guaranteed single picks return the price as WagerTalk credit if the day's package does not show a profit.
Is The Gold Sheet worth it?

As reading material the football paper is cheap at $19 an issue and many long time bettors value it. As a pick service, nothing we could open proves it beats the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays, and the newsletter's own Key Releases were under that mark this season by one forum tally.
